textbookText: A. Tick the correct alternatives: 1. Which region has been identified as one of the world's ten most endangered biodiversity hotspots? a. Upper Amazonia/Guyana Shield b. Congo Basin c. New Guinea/Melanesian Islands d. Himalaya - Nepal

2. What is the primary objective of the IUCN Red List? a. To raise awareness about climate change b. To provide information about species conservation status c. To promote wildlife tourism d. To regulate international wildlife trade
3. Which of the following is listed as an endangered bird species in Nepal? a. Red Panda b. Bengal Tiger c. Great Hornbill d. Himalayan Monal

B. Answer the following questions: 1. Discuss the significance of biodiversity hotspots and the threats they face, with a focus on Nepal's Himalayan region. 2. Define wildlife conservation. 3. What are the major causes of wildlife extinction? 4. Briefly explain the significance of the IUCN Red List. 5. Discuss the importance of wildlife conservation and the major threats faced by wildlife. 6. Explain the key components of the Global Conservation Strategy outlined during the UN Conference on Biodiversity in 1992.

Project work a. Create an engaging poster highlighting urgent conservation needs for specific endangered organisms in Nepal. b. Visit a zoological museum or protected areas, and compile your findings in the form of a report on the existing fauna. c. Investigate innovative strategies for the preservation of biodiversity, developed by countries around the world. ***** Biology, Grade 11 | 499
